chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Allan, from Hammad ibn Isa and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Rib'i ibn Abd Allah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

'Indeed among things are things with leeway and things with constraint. Salat is among those with leeway — it may be prayed early at one time and delayed to another. But the Friday (prayer) is among those with constraint: its time on a Friday is the moment the sun passes its zenith, and the time for Asr on that day corresponds to the time of Zuhr on other days.'

key_terms.سَاعَةُ تَزُولُ: sa'at tazul — the hour of zawal, the precise moment the sun passes its zenith (solar noon)
key_terms.مُضَيَّقَةً: mudayyaqa — things with a narrow/constrained window; applied to obligations with a single fixed moment
key_terms.مُوَسَّعَةً: muwassa'a — things with a wide/flexible time window; applied to prayers that have a range of valid times

ai.seo_question: When is the time for Friday prayer according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a fundamental jurisprudential principle: religious obligations divide into those with flexible timing windows (muwassa'a) and those with strict fixed timings (mudayyaqa). The daily prayers generally allow some flexibility within their prescribed periods, but the Friday congregational prayer has an exceptionally narrow fixed time — precisely at the moment of zawal (solar noon, when the sun passes its zenith). This hadith was foundational for Shia fiqh scholars determining the difference between obligatory and preferred times for salat, with Imam al-Baqir directing this teaching to Fuzayl ibn Yasar, a trusted companion who transmitted legal rulings to the community.
